[Suggestion] A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night (2014), a moody, gorgeous, post-modern vampire film from Iran

I really dig this film. It's set in an Iranian ghost town called Bad City, which is part post-industrial wasteland and part American suburb. Shot in high-contrast black and white, it's a stylish, beautiful film with a great soundtrack and lots of nods to the Spaghetti Western, French Surrealism and New Wave genres. Though it does have romantic elements, it's far more reminiscent of Let The Right One In than the Twilight series.

So now that DTK is out, how do you think the meta will change?

One deck that I really think will be strong is elemental tribal. With the addition of Shorecrasher Elemental, decks based around him, along with Frost Walker, Master of Waves, and Obelisk of Urd will be really strong I think. I personally was going to make a mono-blue elemental tribal, but now I've seen people splashing green for Whisperwood Elemental and the mana ramp for Embodiment of Spring. Embodiment of Spring is one of my favorite cards from Khans, so I might be doing that.

Esper superfriends got way better with the addition of Narset. I also think pretty much anything creature green, like G/W devotion and Temur just got a lot stronger with Deathmist raptor.

I will continue playing U/B control and I will continue running Crux of Fate. One thing I was worried about was that there would be too many good dragons for it to be useful, because people would be mixing dragons and non-dragons. However, looking at the dragons that are actually going to see play, I'm not too worried. I'm really happy about the addition of Ultimate Price, even though it's going to start out in my sideboard.

My younger self would be surprised about the divorce.
What do you think your younger self would say or think about where you are today?
He would probably be pissed about a few pretty shitty decisions I made, but happy that I turned it all around.
Well we all make mistakes, if you can't forgive yourself, who could you ever forgive?

My younger self would probably have a lot to critique about the investments I've made into college education. He thought that it wasn't worth the time commitment when he could start doing the things he loved then. He's not been proved wrong yet, but I've started to love school more, and so he may or may not think I was somewhat whack for that.

College is one of those weird things. It is a very valuable experience. Honestly it is. It just isn't worth a fraction of what it costs, especially for people going out-of-state, or god forbid, to a private university. I could never justify recommending $100k+ in debt to anybody under any circumstances. I can barely avoid debt despite not having to worry about student loans. Financially, it's a fiasco, and people are way better off seeing if they can find another way, be it through family connections or entrepreuneurship. There are a lot more alternatives to college than most would like to admit.

My younger self would Be shocked that I work an office job, but excited that I make enough money to have a high standard of living. I think he would be happy that I'm still married to my highschool sweetheart, which was the best decision I ever made

Well, first off he would be amazed that I made it past 40. It really wasn't part of the plan. He sort of figured that best case scenario was some Mad Max type stuff in a radioactive wasteland. More likely would be dead in an alley by 27.

He would enjoy what I do for a living, and be even happier to learn that along the way he got to live out some of his other dreams.

I'm not sure how he would feel about my SO. He would find her attractive, to be sure, but a lawyer? A wine snob?

I don't think him and my son would get along. My son is too damn nice and well behaved. My younger self would also have no concept of not being into music, or watching videos of people playing video games.

Oh, and since the only video game system he ever owned was an Atari 2600, he would be amazed by my Playstation.
